condition: No cervical screening after total hysterectomy for benign disease
permutationLabel: Age 52, total hysterectomy (cervix removed) for fibroids
summary: 52-year-old woman, total abdominal hysterectomy with removal of the cervix for fibroids 8 years ago, no history of CIN. USPSTF 2018 grade D: no cervical screening. She is due breast and colorectal screening.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Wellness check — which screening tests are due?
inputs.hpi: Asymptomatic 52-year-old at a wellness visit. Total abdominal hysterectomy (uterus and cervix removed) for fibroids 8 years ago; all previous smears normal, never had CIN. Last mammogram 3 years ago. Never had bowel screening.
surgicalHistory: Total abdominal hysterectomy (cervix removed) for fibroids — 8 years ago, benign histology

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Health check — screening review after total hysterectomy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Asymptomatic. Cervical screening not required (total hysterectomy for benign disease, no CIN history). Due mammography and colorectal screening.

mustExclude.note: USPSTF 2018 grade D: no screening after hysterectomy with removal of the cervix for benign disease.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web: cervical_smear fires for every woman 21–65 regardless of surgical history: 'Confirm cervical smear date' and 'Refer gynaecology — cervical smear overdue' after a total hysterectomy for fibroids (USPSTF 2018 grade D).
mustExclude.proposedFix: Suppress cervical_smear when the surgical history records total hysterectomy (cervix removed) for benign disease without CIN 2+.

mustExclude.note: An ACS, PE or AF antithrombotic/thrombolytic plan must never be attached to this diagnosis. Regression guard for DiagnosisRadiationEngine keyword matching: before 999f838 (word-boundary lookup) the first-substring match would have attached the atrial-fibrillation anticoagulation (apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran) plan to this diagnosis because "af" is inside "after". With word-boundary matching no radiation entry matches (simulated from the source), so iOS is expected to pass; to be confirmed on the first iOS CI run.

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for cervical cancer
guideline.section: 21–29: cytology every 3 years; 30–65: cytology every 3 years, high-risk HPV testing alone every 5 years, or co-testing every 5 years (grade A); recommend against screening after hysterectomy with removal of the cervix and no history of CIN 2+ or cancer (grade D)
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for cervical cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2018;320:674–686.

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for breast cancer
guideline.section: Biennial screening mammography for women aged 40–74 (grade B)
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for breast cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2024;331:1918–1930.

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for colorectal cancer
guideline.section: Screen adults 45–49 (grade B) and 50–75 (grade A); 76–85 selectively, considering overall health and prior screening (grade C); stool-based (e.g. annual FIT) or direct visualisation (e.g. colonoscopy every 10 years) strategies
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for colorectal cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2021;325:1965–1977.

rationale: Screening prompts should use the surgical history: after total hysterectomy for benign disease there is no cervix to screen, while breast and colorectal screening are due at 52.
